findings.summary: The list of systems that pull an institution toward extractive normalization lost its explanation.

evidence.baseline: The legal structures, the accounting systems, the employment practices, the strategic planning frameworks are all optimized for extractive institutions, because extractive institutions are the norm and all of these systems evolved to serve them.
evidence.shipped: Capital providers, accounting systems, employment practices, and planning tools all carry assumptions about success.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped sentence says the systems carry assumptions. The baseline says why: they evolved to serve extractive institutions because those are the norm. That is the causal claim the chapter's title depends on, since an attractor without a cause is a metaphor. The shipped clause about becoming legible to the surrounding systems is a real addition and is kept inside the restored sentence.

findings.summary: The constitutional response lost its enumerated mechanism and its limit.

evidence.baseline: A constitutional commitment, embedded in the legal structure, the governance mechanisms, the economic architecture, the data practices, is more resistant, though not immune.
evidence.shipped: Legal form, ownership, governance, funding, and data practice must reinforce the commitment. Constitutional protection can increase resistance, though it cannot make capture impossible.

findings.diagnosis: This one is close, and the shipped version is arguably the better sentence: it adds ownership and states the limit more plainly. Recorded as an intentional retention of the shipped wording inside the restored paragraph rather than as damage. The restoration keeps both the baseline's cultural and constitutional contrast and the shipped enumeration.

findings.summary: Credit, running the other way. The kept legibility clause names the mechanism of extractive normalization that the baseline's list only gestures at.

evidence.baseline: An institution that begins with a commitment to non-extractive operation will find, as it grows, that every system it encounters pulls it toward extractive normalization.
evidence.shipped: An institution that begins with a commitment to non-extractive operation will find, as it grows, that every system it encounters pulls it toward extractive normalization, sometimes simply so that it can remain legible to the systems around it.

findings.authorizedBy: R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, recorded in the twenty-rule audit of 2026-07-31. The original record's regeneration note states the section is the volume's first case of a shipped sentence kept on the merits.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline says the pull exists; the clause says why an institution yields without anyone intending extraction, which is the chapter's own thesis that the attractor is structural rather than moral. The clause completes the argument it is attached to.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Three em dashes. Two were parenthetical enumerations and became comma pairs. One introduced a specification of the metrics markets reward and became a comma pair, the enclosed list already carrying commas being read as an appositive series.
The shipped enumeration of legal form, ownership, governance, funding, and data practice, and the shipped statement of the limit. Both are better than the baseline's equivalents.
The causal account of why the surrounding systems pull toward extraction, and the cultural versus constitutional contrast.

openQuestions: The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section is the first in the volume where a shipped sentence is better than its baseline counterpart and is kept on the merits. Recording a retention as a decision is what stops the next pass from reverting it, and the standard requires the record to say so.

audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the cultural versus constitutional contrast keeps both the committing claim and the limit, more resistant, though not immune. R-PAIRED-DELETION: extractive attractor is defined here and used through Parts II and VI; the defining end is intact. R-REGISTER-DICTION: the divergence from the baseline's HR practices to employment practices is now attributed; the generic institutional register is the volume's own and the abbreviation was from nowhere. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK, R-REFRAIN-COST: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Ten of fourteen baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder trace to three recorded punctuation repairs and the two attributed retentions. One substitution credit recorded as F3. No prose change required.
corrections: Two divergences now attributed: HR practices stands as employment practices under R-REGISTER-DICTION, and the normalization sentence carries the kept shipped clause sometimes simply so that it can remain legible to the systems around it, which the original record kept on the merits.
